previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___, a patient with multiple myeloma, COPD, CAD, and a history of recent pneumonia and neck pain, was readmitted after his daughter noticed erythema and a healed ulcer on his right great toe. He denied pain or fever. He was admitted for IV antibiotics due to risk of infection from immunocompromise and prior gangrene. He received IV vancomycin, and podiatry performed a debridement, finding no deep infection. A foot X-ray showed no osteomyelitis. He was found to be dehydrated with acute kidney injury, improved with IV fluids. Anemia was managed with one unit of PRBCs. Levofloxacin was discontinued due to drowsiness and myoclonus, with transition to cefpodoxime and azithromycin for pneumonia. A PICC line was placed for outpatient IV antibiotics. He was discharged home with home infusion, improved cellulitis, and stable vital signs.

Brief Hospital Course:
Mr. ___ is a ___ year old male with multiple medical problems 
including multiple myeloma, CAD, a-fib, and COPD who presents 
with increasing lethargy, decreased PO, confusion, and SOB x 2 
days  
.  
# Pneumonia: On admission, a new reticular opacity was seen in 
the LUL. Chest CT confirmed infection of the LUL as well as 
infiltrate in the superior portion of the LLL. The prior LLL 
opacity had largely resolved. He was initially started on 
Vancomycin, cefepime, and azithromycin. He improved on IV 
antibiotics and was transitioned to cefpodoxime and azithromycin 
to complete a 14-day course upon discharge. He also received a 
dose of IVIG. ID saw the patient and recommended flu and 
pneumococcal vaccine, smoking cessation, IVIG every ___ weeks 
during respiratory viral season, and possibly prophylaxis with 
azithromycin or erythromycin. He was also given scheduled 
nebulizers for COPD/wheezing during admission and was 
transitioned to his home inhalers upon discharge.  
. 
# AMS: Patient was extremely lethargic and oriented x 2 on 
admission - a change from baseline. He improved by HD#2 after 
the initiation of antibiotics and decompression of his bladder. 
A Head CT was obtained and was negative. 
. 
# Elevated INR: The patient had recently stopped Coumadin due to 
thrombocytopenia. Despite this, his INR was elevated to 2 on 
admission. Vit K was given. Aspirin was held and platelets were 
transfused. 
. 
# Urinary retention: The patient has a history of bladder cancer 
s/p formation of a neobladder. He had recently been seen in 
___ clinic where it was recommended that he perform CIC. He 
had not been self-cathing at home. On admission, he was 
straight-cath'd, which returned 2.5L in urine. It was 
recommended that he resume CIC upon discharge.  
. 
# Multiple Myeloma: Last IgG 3769; this was repeated on 
admission and was 2944. He had recently started lenalidomide 
about a week PTA and was restarted on this the day prior to 
discharge. He was schedule for hematology f/u the week following 
discharge. 
. 
# Arrhythmia: On admission, the patient was in Aflutter vs. 
coarse afib. He was placed on telemetry. Enzymes were flat. 
Telemetry revealed occasional <10 beat runs of NSVT as well as 
sinus bradycardia. He was continued on Toprol XL 25 mg qday. He 
was scheduled with cardiology follow-up. Aspirin and Coumadin 
were held until follow-up appointment when Plt trend would be 
better understood.

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  ___ male with history of multiple myeloma, on
chemotherapy, presents with dyspnea.  Evaluate for pneumonia.

COMPARISON:  ___.

FRONTAL AND LATERAL VIEWS OF THE CHEST:  There is new reticular opacity in the
left upper lobe, concerning for pneumonia.  There is no pleural effusion or
pneumothorax.  Cardiomediastinal silhouette is unchanged from prior.  Hilar
contours and pulmonary vasculature are normal. Mid-thoracic compression
deformities are similar to prior. Old right distal clavicular fracture is
noted.

Findings discussed with Dr. ___ at 12 pm on ___.

HISTORY:  A ___ male with multiple medical problems including multiple
myeloma, COPD who presents with lethargy, confusion, shortness of breath and
reticular infiltrate on chest x-ray and left upper lobe.

COMPARISON:  Prior chest x-ray dated ___ and chest CT dated
___.

TECHNIQUE:  Contiguous helical acquisition through the chest was performed
without intravenous contrast.  1.25 and 5-mm axial and sagittal and coronally
reformatted images were created.

FINDINGS:  New ground-glass opacification and interlobular septal thickening
involves the apical posterior segment of the left upper lobe, the superior
segment of the left lower lobe and extends into the lingula where there is a
dense area of consolidation peripherally.  The previous left lower lobe
consolidation has nearly completely resolved except for some residual
ground-glass opacity.

Diffuse emphysema persists.  The previously noted lingular nodule measuring 9
mm is obscured by the consolidation in the lingula.  A 3mm right middle lobe
nodule along the major fissure (4:145) previously measured 5mm, and a 2-mm
nodule (4:182) along the major fissure has also decreased in size, previously
measuring 8 mm.  No new nodules are identified.

The heart is normal in size.  There is dense atherosclerotic calcification of
the coronary arteries and two right coronary artery stents.  Mediastinal lymph
nodes are prominent in appearance measuring 9 mm in the prevascular space,
previously 3 mm, and up to 6 mm in the left paratracheal region, previously 4
mm.  No pathologically enlarged mediastinal or hilar lymphadenopathy is noted.
The tracheobronchial tree is patent to level of the subsegmental bronchi
bilaterally.  No pleural or pericardial effusions are present.  

The bones are diffusely mottled, particularly the ribs, consistent with
multiple myeloma.  A right clavicular fracture is partially imaged but
unchanged.  Right ninth and left eighth rib fractures are healed.  Chronic
compression fractures of the T7 and T8 vertebral bodies are stable.

Although this study was not designed for subdiaphragmatic evaluation, a 6-mm
low-density lesion in the right lobe of the liver is stable.  No additional
abnormalities are seen.

IMPRESSION:

1.  New dense consolidation in the lingula and ground-glass opacity and
interlobular septal thickening involving the left upper lobe and superior
segment of the left lower lobe.  Findings are consistent with pneumonia with
or without possible surrounding hemorrhage.  Mildly prominent mediastinal
lymph nodes, likely reactive in nature.

2.  Moderate diffuse emphysema.

3.  Interval decrease in size of two perifissural nodules as described above.

4.  Chronic rib and clavicular fractures and underlying bony myeloma changes.

5.  Interval near complete resolution of left lower lobe dense consolidation
with mild residual ground-glass opacity noted.

These findings were communciated to Dr. ___ on ___ at 5:45 pm.

HISTORY:  ___ male with increasing lethargy, decreased oral intake,
confusion, shortness of breath; also with elevated INR and thrombocytopenia on
aspirin.  History of multiple myeloma, CAD, COPD.

STUDY:  CT of the head without contrast.

COMPARISON:  ___.

FINDINGS:  The lower portion of the head was scanned multiple times due to
motion.  There is no evidence of intracranial hemorrhage, edema or mass
effect.  The gray-white matter differentiation is preserved.  The ventricles
and sulci are mildly prominent due to mild cerebral atrophy. 

Mild to moderate mucosal thickening and aerosolized secretions are present in
the left maxillary sinus.

IMPRESSION:
1.  No intracranial hemorrhage or evidence of other acute intracranial
abnormalities.
2.  Left maxillary sinus disease.  The presence of aerosolized secretions
could indicate acute sinusitis.  Please correlate clinically.
